title: How to use MCP Tasks and Elicitations in Claude Code
partialText: Build a local MCP server with background tasks and confirmation forms in Claude Code. Learn how polling, cancellation, and reconnecting work.

title: The complete guide to Convex
partialText: Learn Convex by building a real-time app with TypeScript, queries, mutations, authentication, indexes, search, file storage, background jobs, and tests.

title: How to use Grok Build
partialText: A detailed Grok Build tutorial covering installation, prompts, plans, permissions, tests, Git, skills, MCP, subagents, sessions, and headless automation.

title: A pull request workflow for code written by agents
partialText: Review agent-written code with a practical pull request workflow: focused tests, independent review, human approval, merge queues, and deployment checks.

title: Prompt caching, compression, and compaction in coding agents
partialText: Learn how prompt caching, transport compression, and context compaction affect coding agent costs, speed, memory, and usage, with practical examples.

title: Pushing to main still needs a process
partialText: Direct pushes can keep development simple, but trust needs concrete checks. Look at access, traceability, tests, and recovery before copying a team's workflow.

title: What changes when you stop opening the code editor?
partialText: Coding agents can move work outside the editor. Understanding changes, reproducing bugs, and checking the application still need a place in the workflow.

title: Cloudflare Hyperdrive tutorial: use PostgreSQL with Workers
partialText: Learn Cloudflare Hyperdrive with PostgreSQL and Workers, configure pooling and caching, and see how it fits with D1, R2, Queues, Supabase, and Neon.

title: What teaching can tell us about prompting
partialText: Clear examples and useful feedback help when teaching a concept or directing a coding agent. Explain the expected behavior and show where the result differs.

title: Too many conversations with coding agents
partialText: Several coding agent chats can leave decisions scattered across sessions. Keep one place for the current task, and give parallel work a clear handoff.

title: Software with a point of view
partialText: A software maker's taste shows up in defaults, empty states, and ordinary interactions. Give your app character through decisions that help people use it.

title: What would make an overnight agent useful?
partialText: An overnight coding agent needs a question worth answering. Start with the decision its result will help you make, and keep the morning review manageable.

title: I care more about the AI product I can use
partialText: An impressive AI roadmap means little when the product you need is unavailable. A practical way to separate future promises from today's useful software.

title: How to use Cursor Computer Use
partialText: Use Cursor Computer Use to test desktop apps and iOS Simulator flows, reproduce UI bugs, and verify fixes with clear prompts and expected results.

title: The complete guide to LM Studio Bionic
partialText: Learn LM Studio Bionic: choose local or cloud models, fix a JavaScript bug step by step, work with documents, and review what the agent changes.

title: How to secure a VPS with Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel
partialText: Secure a VPS with private SSH over Tailscale and public web traffic through Cloudflare Tunnel. A complete guide to setup, firewalls, testing, and recovery.

title: What to check before submitting a native app to App Review
partialText: Prepare an Apple app for review, choose useful native interactions, adopt Liquid Glass, and understand how direct Mac distribution differs.

title: Triage support tickets in one request with OpenAI's Decisions API
partialText: OpenAI's Decisions API returns a probability, a choice, or a score. Triage a support ticket with several questions in one request.

title: How to publish a Chrome extension to the Chrome Web Store
partialText: Publish your Chrome extension with a clean ZIP, store listing, privacy disclosures, permission justifications, review instructions, and tested updates.

title: What to check before upgrading the Anthropic SDK
partialText: Upgrading the Anthropic SDK changes the API version your app sends. Check sampling parameters, authentication, message history, and output before you ship.

title: How to use a coding agent without another subscription
partialText: Connect OpenCode to DeepSeek or Ollama, understand API billing and local hardware costs, and test whether the setup works for your projects.

title: How to create a DMG installer for a Mac app
partialText: Package your Mac app in a drag-to-Applications DMG, sign and notarize it, verify the download, and attach it to a GitHub release.

title: AI video editing tools: what agents need to work safely
partialText: Recording and editing tools need inspectable state, useful commands, and recoverable changes if we want agents to help with real creative work.

title: A deep dive into Claude Duet
partialText: Claude Duet is Anthropic's proactive cloud agent. Learn how it works, what it can access, and how it compares with Grok Bot and ChatGPT dots.

title: Paid traffic for SaaS validation: how to test product demand
partialText: How to use a small paid traffic experiment to learn who gets value from a product, measure useful actions, and decide what to change.

title: How to protect your app from AI-powered attacks
partialText: Protect your app from AI-powered attacks with practical advice on patching, access controls, security log monitoring, backups, and incident response.

title: Give your coding agent a state machine
partialText: Build a small JavaScript state machine for a coding agent, with explicit transitions, a retry limit, a useful event log, and tests.

title: PSA: update PHP today
partialText: PHP security fixes are available. Update now, check the fixed versions, and use these temporary mitigations only while waiting for patched packages.

title: Jev vs structured outputs: when to use each
partialText: Compare Jev, JSON mode, and schema-constrained LLM outputs. Learn when a typed answer is enough and when decision probabilities justify another model.

title: Vite toolchain: Cloudflare, vinext, and shared web tooling
partialText: Vite is becoming shared infrastructure for frameworks, runtimes, and developer tools. What vinext, Cloudflare's new tooling, and DevTools show.
